rapport_notes: Friendly and responsive but somewhat procedural; no real warmth or personalization, purely transactional.
process_discipline_notes: No violations detected; no items repeated, and no silence-holding requirement was explicitly triggered after open questions (agenda was never asked, so no silence-hold test applied there).

evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep launches straight into "What day this week? We're in the is this a house or an apartment?" with no framing or time-boxed ask.
evidence_quotes.agenda: Never asked. Rep moves directly to logistics (address, square footage, bedrooms, packing) without asking about concerns or priorities.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — no concerns raised because the agenda question was never asked.
evidence_quotes.sheet1_careful_with: Mentioned in Stage 3: "we also include a bunch of stuff with damage protection so you get $2,000 allocated for every single move and damage protection."
evidence_quotes.sheet2_whos_coming: Never mentioned. No reference to who will show up, crew lead, team makeup, or Meet Your Mover.
evidence_quotes.communication: Not covered anywhere. No mention of day-before call, crew lead contact, or inbox updates.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Partial. Rep gives a range ("generally a house like this is gonna take anywhere from like six to eight hours") but doesn't explicitly personalize it to factors mentioned (e.g., "because of the hour drive and three bedrooms"). Later estimates 4 + 1 + 2–3 = roughly 8 hours, but framing is post-hoc rather than anchored upfront.
evidence_quotes.estimate_is_a_window: "Basically, right now the and again just remember this will be for two trucks... we always try to air on the side of caution." Also: "if you get some more context we would love to, to make it a little bit cheaper."
evidence_quotes.close: No rate-lock statement. No explicit ask ("would you like our help with your move?"). Call ends with "All you need obviously the move is this coming week. So the sooner you let us know the better chance will still be available."

top_strength: Excellent logistics capture and multi-option thinking—rep offered both a two-truck and one-truck alternative, clearly explained pricing structure ($404/hr + $230 travel fee), and invited customer to send photos for refinement, showing customer-centric problem-solving.
coaching_note: Lead with the agenda question (concerns + priorities) before diving into logistics, and always close with an explicit rate-lock and ask for the business ("would you like us to help?") rather than just handing off the quote.
